pages.title: IVF and fertility care in Saipan
pages.description: Explore IVF, ICSI, fertility preservation, the medical team and the practical steps for arranging care in Saipan.
sections: Understand your treatment options
Compare IVF, ICSI, egg freezing and frozen embryo transfer. Begin with your goals and existing reports; a physician determines which options are appropriate.
Know who provides your care
Review the institution’s public team information, then confirm your treating physician, clinic location and appointment arrangements.
Plan treatment and travel separately
Review the treatment schedule and written fee scope before booking flights or accommodation. Retrieval and transfer may be arranged in different stages.
Questions before you begin
How much should you budget? How long can treatment take? Can you ask for advice without recent reports? Find direct answers and their sources in the FAQ.

about.title: About Saipan IVF and care coordination
about.description: Understand the roles of consultation, appointment coordination and the institution providing medical treatment.
sections: Information and appointment coordination
This website helps you understand fertility options and prepare questions for the receiving institution. The consultation form creates an email draft for the institution’s published email address.
Medical responsibility

Examinations, diagnosis, prescriptions, egg retrieval, laboratory procedures and embryo transfer are the responsibility of the receiving medical team. Confirm the institution, physician and service agreement before booking.
Separate medical and coordination fees

Confirm who receives each payment, which services are included and how cancellations or changes are settled. Accommodation, transport, obstetric care and third-party services are separate arrangements.
Clinic location
The institution publishes its name as Saipan IVF Center and its address as 3rd Floor, Bank of Guam, Garapan, Saipan, MP 96950. Confirm the precise appointment location before travelling.

team.title: Medical team and embryology laboratory
team.description: Meet the professionals listed on the institution’s public team page and prepare questions about your own care.
sections: Gary G. Ramsey, M.D. — Medical Director

The institution lists him as Medical Director and states that his medical degree is from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA). Confirm who will conduct your consultation and explain your treatment options.
Irena Lalic — Embryology specialist

The institution states that her MSc in Biology is from the University of Zagreb and her MSc in Clinical Embryology is from the University of Leeds. Ask when fertilisation, culture and freezing reports are provided and who explains them.
Rose Wang — Head Nurse
The institution lists Rose Wang as Head Nurse. Ask how medication instructions, appointment preparation and follow-up communications are coordinated.
Laboratory and facilities

The institution’s facilities page describes micromanipulation systems, embryo workstations, MIRI® IVF incubators and oocyte vitrification. Confirm the actual treatment location, laboratory arrangements and procedures available for your plan.
Confirm your appointment team
Public profiles do not establish a current appointment or roster. Request the name and professional registration information of the clinician who will actually provide your care.

treatments.title: Fertility treatments and preservation
treatments.description: Compare IVF, ICSI, egg freezing and frozen embryo transfer, and understand related donor and family-building consultations.
sections: Choose a starting point
IVF covers a broader treatment process; ICSI changes the laboratory fertilisation step. Egg freezing preserves eggs for possible future use, while FET uses existing frozen embryos.
Sperm freezing and donor options

Sperm freezing, donated eggs or sperm, and third-party family-building involve separate screening, resource availability, consent and document requirements. Discuss your circumstances with the receiving institution.
Single people and LGBTQ+ families
Explain your family-building goals first. Medical eligibility, donor resources, third-party involvement, parentage documents and cross-border requirements need individual confirmation.

process.title: Your IVF consultation and care journey
process.description: Prepare for consultation, assessment, a written plan, treatment and follow-up, one stage at a time.
sections: 1. Initial enquiry
Share your main interests, previous treatment, departure city and preferred timing. Confirm the consultation channel, format, fee and information required for assessment.
2. Organise reports and history

Sort existing reports by date and summarise treatment, surgery, medication and allergies. Confirm a suitable submission channel; the receiving clinician decides which reports remain usable and what needs repeating.
3. Physician assessment
Discuss treatment choices, alternatives, risks and monitoring. Obtain an individual plan, examination requirements and a list of unresolved questions.
4. Written fees and travel
Confirm the care provider, payment recipient, included services, exclusions and cancellation terms. Book travel against the clinic’s appointment dates and review change policies.
5. Treatment at the clinic

Bring the documents requested by the clinic. The medical team manages diagnosis, medication, monitoring, retrieval, culture or transfer. Obtain the reports and follow-up instructions relevant to the treatment performed.
6. Return and follow-up
Keep your treatment summary, prescriptions, payment records and storage authorisations. Confirm review dates, communication channels, storage renewal and whom to contact if you need care.
Treatment length is not the same as length of stay

An IVF cycle is commonly described as approximately 3–6 weeks, depending on the protocol and stages included. This does not mean you must stay in Saipan throughout. Retrieval and frozen transfer may require separate arrangements.
Before booking flights

Keep four confirmations: your institution and clinician; monitoring, appointment and return dates; written fee and cancellation terms; and contact details during treatment and after returning home. Verify permitted immigration stay separately.

fees.title: IVF fees and budget planning
fees.description: Separate retrieval and culture, medication, laboratory procedures, transfer, storage and travel costs before comparing quotations.
sections: Base price and combined budget

The $15,000 base reference covers retrieval and culture. The default $26,100–31,100 combination adds medication, anaesthesia, ICSI, freezing and one frozen transfer; it does not cover every possible expense.
Before payment
Request the currency, included procedures and number of services, additional items, payment recipient, payment stages and cancellation or postponement terms in writing.
Costs outside the calculator

Initial tests, transfer medication, transport, accommodation, extra cycles, complication management and unselected items are excluded. Donor and third-party services need separate scope and contracts.

guides.title: Patient guides
guides.description: Find the right information for first consultation, treatment comparison, travel preparation and follow-up.
sections: New to fertility care?
Start with the first-consultation guide, meet the medical team and prepare a concise list of questions. You do not need to select a treatment yourself.
Comparing treatment and costs
Read the IVF stages, compare the treatment pages, then use the budget tool and quotation checklist to align what each price includes.
Preparing to travel or return home
Confirm your appointment, documents and payment terms before arranging travel. Keep your medication instructions, review dates and storage contact details after treatment.

guides/first-visit.title: Your first consultation: what to prepare
guides/first-visit.description: Organise the reports you already have and confirm the consultation format before arranging additional tests.
sections: Start with four details
State your area of interest, previous treatment, departure city and preferred timing. If you are unsure about treatment, say so rather than choosing a protocol yourself.
Organise existing reports

Sort laboratory, ultrasound, semen analysis and previous stimulation or transfer records by date. Include a medication, allergy and surgery summary. Preserve names, dates, units and reference ranges rather than sending isolated results.
No recent reports? You can still enquire

Ask whether consultation is remote or in person, what it costs and which records the clinician needs. Wait for the clinic’s list before arranging tests that may duplicate existing information or expire.
Send records through a confirmed channel
Use the first email for a short question summary. Confirm the institution, privacy arrangements and designated submission method before sending full medical records.
After sending your enquiry

Confirm the actual physician, appointment format and date, accepted reports, further tests, consultation fee and quotation process. Generating a draft is not sending it, and a booking requires an explicit reply.

guides/ivf-steps.title: The main stages of an IVF cycle
guides/ivf-steps.description: Understand assessment, stimulation, egg retrieval, fertilisation, culture, transfer and follow-up.
sections: Assessment and planning
The clinician reviews your history and reports, discusses treatment choices and explains monitoring and medication. Confirm which stages can be completed locally and which require attendance.
Stimulation and monitoring
Use medication only as prescribed and attend the requested ultrasound or blood tests. Monitoring results may change the timing of later appointments.
Retrieval, fertilisation and culture

The medical team arranges egg retrieval and laboratory fertilisation. Conventional IVF and ICSI are different fertilisation methods; ask why a particular method is proposed and when results are communicated.
Transfer or freezing
A fresh transfer, embryo freezing or later frozen transfer depends on the individual plan and results. Not every cycle produces embryos suitable for transfer.
Follow-up and timing
Obtain a medication schedule, test dates, treatment summary and contact details. A general 3–6 week cycle estimate is not a universal travel or pregnancy timetable.

guides/quotation.title: How to read an IVF quotation
guides/quotation.description: Compare scope, additional items, payment stages and cancellation terms before comparing totals.
sections: Identify the service and payment recipient
Check the institution, clinician, currency, quotation date and validity. Medical fees, coordination, accommodation, transport and third-party services may have different providers.
Compare the same scope
Identify whether monitoring, retrieval, standard fertilisation, ICSI, anaesthesia, culture, freezing and transfer are included, and how many times each service is covered.
Medication, testing and storage

Ask how medication quantities are charged, whether PGT-related biopsy, sample transport and testing are included, and when annual storage starts. Future use of frozen eggs has additional steps and costs.
Cancellation or additional treatment
Before payment, obtain the settlement rules for a cancelled cycle, postponement, no usable eggs, no transferable embryos and additional procedures.
Use the budget tool as a checklist
Adjust the relevant items, then request a personal written quotation. The tool does not decide which procedures you need and does not include all treatment or travel costs.

guides/egg-freezing.title: Preparing for an egg-freezing consultation
guides/egg-freezing.description: Discuss assessment, retrieval, freezing, annual storage and possible future use as separate decisions.
sections: Discuss your goals and available time
Explain why you are considering preservation, when you can attend and any relevant medical history or medication. Bring existing reports; the clinician decides which assessment is required.
Understand the cycle
Ask where monitoring occurs, how retrieval and anaesthesia are arranged, and when the clinic provides the number of eggs frozen and the storage report.
Separate present and future costs

The reference base cycle is $9,000. Initial checks, medication, anaesthesia and annual storage are additional. Later thawing, fertilisation, culture and transfer need a separate assessment and budget.
Confirm storage arrangements
Keep the storage provider, consent documents, renewal fee and contact details. Ask what to do if your contact information changes, you wish to transfer samples or you stop storage.
Understand the limits

Egg freezing preserves a possibility, not a guarantee of future pregnancy or birth. Discuss the expected outcome and limitations for your circumstances rather than relying on a single headline success rate.

guides/travel-checklist.title: Cross-border treatment travel checklist
guides/travel-checklist.description: Align appointments, entry documents, flights, accommodation and follow-up before travelling.
sections: Confirm your medical dates first
Obtain the receiving institution, physician, address, consultation date, monitoring plan and estimated return arrangements. Treatment changes may require rescheduling.
Verify the correct entry pathway
Check requirements for your passport, genuine purpose of travel and intended stay. An authorisation does not guarantee admission, and treatment duration is separate from permitted stay.
Book flexible transport and accommodation
Review cancellation terms, the distance to the clinic, local transport, accompanying-person needs and accessibility. Keep room for appointment changes.
Carry the requested records
Bring the clinic’s confirmation, relevant reports, prescriptions and other requested documents. Confirm how the institution will receive sensitive records before sending them.
Before returning home
Keep the treatment summary, medication and review instructions, payment records and any storage authorisation. Confirm follow-up contacts and where to seek medical help if needed.

guides/family-planning.title: Questions about donor and third-party family-building
guides/family-planning.description: Clarify medical eligibility, available resources, costs and documents before selecting a pathway.
sections: Explain your family-building goals
Single people and LGBTQ+ families can begin by describing their circumstances and the questions they want answered. Available options require individual assessment.
Donor eggs or sperm
Ask about available samples, screening records, receiving criteria, consent, waiting times, transport and storage. Public service descriptions do not guarantee a particular resource is available.
Third-party involvement

Medical services, third-party arrangements, legal advice and parentage documents are separate matters. Confirm who provides and charges for each service, and which documents apply to the places involved.
Before committing funds
Obtain a written scope, payment recipient, cancellation terms and the responsibilities of each participant. Keep IVF, obstetric care, birth registration and immigration arrangements separate.

birth-planning.title: Birth in Saipan and family planning
birth-planning.description: Citizenship, education and family arrangements. Fertility treatment and childbirth are separate plans.
sections: Birth citizenship

Under the longstanding rule described in State Department 8 FAM 302.2, people born in the Northern Mariana Islands on or after 4 November 1986 acquire US citizenship at birth under Covenant section 303. Check the rules, court orders and parental-status exceptions effective when applying.
Nationality and travel documents

Your home country may have its own rules on nationality for children born abroad, including whether dual nationality is recognised and what travel documents are required. Confirm the child’s status, passport options and any declaration or choice requirements with your country’s competent authority.
Travel and social benefits

Passport entry arrangements change by destination. Visa-free entry is not permission to work or settle. A Social Security number alone does not confer benefits; health coverage and pensions have separate eligibility and contribution requirements.
School and university

US public primary and secondary schools generally do not charge tuition, subject to residence, district and age requirements. University admission, aid and in-state tuition are assessed separately; citizenship does not guarantee admission or a fixed discount.
Working in the United States
US citizens generally do not need a work visa, but licensing, age, qualification and security requirements may apply. A child’s citizenship does not give parents work authorisation.
Obstetric and childbirth care
Arrange the receiving hospital, obstetric clinician, pain-relief options, insurance and self-pay scope separately. Available delivery methods depend on medical assessment and the provider’s services.
Accommodation and local resources
Review housing, food, clinic access, transport, local medical resources and referral arrangements. A comfortable environment does not itself mean lower medical risk.
Schooling after returning home

Check your home country’s entry rules for compulsory schooling and any documents needed for a child born overseas. University admission as an international student is assessed separately and may include nationality, passport duration, overseas residence and institutional requirements.
Immigration for parents

A US citizen aged 21 or older can petition for parents. This immediate-relative category is not subject to an annual visa quota, but application, financial sponsorship and admissibility requirements remain; permanent residence is not automatic.

service-scope.title: Appointments and service responsibilities
service-scope.description: Confirm the medical provider, coordination scope, payment recipient and written terms before booking.
sections: Initial consultation
Confirm the reply channel, language, remote or in-person format and consultation fee. An enquiry or email draft is not a confirmed medical appointment.
Appointment and travel coordination
Clarify who handles records, booking dates, accommodation, transport and schedule changes, and whether coordination is charged separately.
Clinical and laboratory care
Confirm the receiving institution, treating physician and actual procedure location. Diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment and interpretation of results belong to the medical team.
Documents before payment

Obtain the service and payment recipient details, personal written plan and quote, included and excluded items, service counts, validity, payment stages, receipts and cancellation or postponement terms.
Aftercare and storage
Confirm whom to contact about medication, reviews, treatment records, sample storage, authorisations and renewal payments.
Separate services
IVF, obstetric delivery, accommodation, meals, transport, donor resources, third-party arrangements and legal documents are not one service. Check who provides each item and whether it is included.

editorial-policy.title: Sources, content and image credits
editorial-policy.description: Understand how patient information, reference budgets and institution-sourced images are presented.
sections: Medical and policy sources

Patient information refers to HFEA, NHS and ASRM materials where linked. Citizenship and travel information links to the US State Department and CBP. Read the relevant source and check current requirements for your situation.
Institution information

Names, location, team profiles and publicly described facilities are attributed to the receiving institution’s website. Public profiles are not independent verification of a current licence, appointment or equipment availability.
Fees and treatment outcomes

Amounts are reference budgets, not a confirmed personal package. Request a written quote. Research outcomes apply to their study populations and must not be presented as the receiving institution’s success rates.
Images

Team and building images are attributed to the institution. Other editorial photographs illustrate topics and do not establish that a person, laboratory or interior is a patient or facility of the receiving institution.
Updates and corrections
Medical evidence, service availability and administrative rules can change. For corrections or source questions, contact the published institution email and identify the relevant page and wording.

privacy.title: Privacy and use of the consultation form
privacy.description: Learn how the email draft is generated, who receives it and how to submit personal records.
sections: How the form works

The form assembles your input in your browser. Generating a draft does not send it; open your own email application or copy the text, review the recipient and content, then send it yourself. This website has no submission endpoint receiving the form.
Who receives your email
The default recipient is the institution’s published address, info@saipan-ivf.com. After sending, your email provider and the receiving institution handle it under their own rules.
What to include

Include one way to reach you. Your name, area of interest, timing and questions are optional. Contact details are included in the email; generating a draft does not upload them to a website backend or save them to browser storage. Start with your area of interest, timing and main questions. Do not include identity-document numbers, complete medical records or another person’s information without consent in the initial enquiry. Confirm a designated channel before sending detailed records.
Hosting and external links

Cloudflare Pages hosts these static pages. Hosting, network and email providers may process necessary access or communication information under their policies. External links are governed by the destination’s rules.
Appointments and payment

Reading a page or generating an email does not create a medical booking, treatment contract or payment obligation. Actual service documents govern the appointment, treatment, price, cancellation terms and data authorisations.

contact.title: Contact and first consultation
contact.description: One contact method is enough to start. Your name, treatment interests and questions are optional; you can also email directly.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Direct answers about treatment, fees, timing, travel and citizenship, with linked sources.

treatments.title: IVF — in vitro fertilisation
treatments.summary: Eggs and sperm are combined outside the body, and an embryo may later be transferred into the uterus. A clinician considers the cause of infertility, previous treatment and examination results.
treatments.suitable: IVF may be discussed for tubal problems, some ovulation or sperm factors, or unexplained infertility after other treatment. Ask which alternatives remain appropriate.
stages: Egg retrieval, fertilisation and embryo culture
Transfer or freezing, followed by review
treatments.included: Routine monitoring, one retrieval, conventional fertilisation and embryo culture.
treatments.excluded: Initial tests, stimulation medication, anaesthesia, ICSI, freezing, annual storage, genetic testing, transfer and living expenses.
treatments.risk: Discuss ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, multiple pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, cycle cancellation and the possibility of no usable eggs or transferable embryos. Compare live-birth rates using the same denominator; a positive pregnancy test is not a live birth.
questions: Why is this plan appropriate, and what alternatives exist?
Where is monitoring performed and how many visits are required?
How are cancellation, postponement or no transferable embryos charged?

treatments.title: ICSI — intracytoplasmic sperm injection
treatments.summary: An embryologist injects one sperm into an egg. ICSI changes the fertilisation step within IVF; it is not a complete treatment cycle or a universal way to improve live-birth rates.
treatments.suitable: It may be discussed for significant sperm abnormalities or previous poor or failed fertilisation. Ask what finding supports its use instead of conventional fertilisation.
stages: Review semen analysis and prior fertilisation records
Coordinate sperm preparation, retrieval and injection
treatments.included: The ICSI laboratory procedure, listed separately.
treatments.excluded: The full IVF cycle, medication, anaesthesia, retrieval, culture, storage and transfer.
treatments.risk: An egg can be damaged during micromanipulation. Injection does not guarantee fertilisation, a transferable embryo or live birth. The wider stimulation, retrieval and transfer risks still apply.
questions: Is the charge per cycle or based on egg numbers?
Who explains fertilisation and culture results?

treatments.title: Egg freezing and fertility preservation
treatments.summary: Eggs are retrieved and frozen for possible future use. This preserves an option and does not guarantee a future pregnancy or birth.
treatments.suitable: Discuss your preservation goals, future plans, existing history and medication. The clinician determines which assessment and cycle arrangements are appropriate.
stages: Assessment and review of existing reports
Renewal and authorisation for possible future use
treatments.included: Routine monitoring, one retrieval and freezing.
treatments.excluded: Initial tests, medication, anaesthesia and annual storage. Future thawing, fertilisation, culture and transfer are separately assessed and charged.
treatments.risk: Discuss stimulation and retrieval risks, the possibility of few or no suitable eggs, and the limitations of future survival, fertilisation and pregnancy outcomes. Age and individual factors matter.
questions: What outcome and limitations should I expect from one cycle?
Are freezing and annual storage charged separately?
What happens if I change contact details, transfer samples or stop storage?

treatments.title: FET — frozen embryo transfer
treatments.summary: An existing frozen embryo is thawed for transfer. Embryo records, authorisations and individual medical circumstances determine whether and how a transfer can proceed.
treatments.suitable: Consider this page if you already have frozen embryos or are planning a later transfer. Embryos held by another institution require acceptance and transport arrangements first.
stages: Check embryo records, storage provider and authorisations
Confirm preparation, monitoring, medication and attendance
Pregnancy testing, medication instructions and follow-up
treatments.included: Routine monitoring, thawing and one transfer.
treatments.excluded: Transfer medication, annual storage, sample transport, additional tests and other procedures.
treatments.risk: Not every embryo survives thawing or results in pregnancy. Discuss cancellation, the number transferred, multiple pregnancy and follow-up with the clinical team.
questions: Do the existing embryo records meet receiving requirements?
What is my preparation plan and attendance schedule?
How are thawing, cancellation and postponement charged?

faq: Is a child born in Saipan a US citizen?
Under the longstanding birth-citizenship rule, generally yes: a citizen, rather than a green-card holder.

State Department 8 FAM 302.2 describes citizenship at birth in the Northern Mariana Islands on or after 4 November 1986 under Covenant section 303. Check administrative measures, court orders and parental-status exceptions effective when applying for registration and a passport.
Does IVF in Saipan itself confer US citizenship?
No. The place of IVF treatment and the place of birth are different matters.
Retrieval, embryo culture or transfer in Saipan does not itself give an embryo, child or parents US citizenship. Childbirth, obstetric costs and entry documents must be planned separately.
Do parents automatically receive green cards?
No. A child’s citizenship does not automatically grant parents residence or work authorisation.
A US citizen aged 21 or older may petition for parents in the immediate-relative category without an annual visa quota. Applications, financial sponsorship and admissibility requirements still apply.
Do I need a visa to visit Saipan?
Eligible travellers from Visa Waiver Program countries may use ESTA for US visits of up to 90 days. Eligible Chinese citizens have a separate CNMI EVS-TAP route for visits of up to 14 days.

ESTA and CNMI EVS-TAP are different programmes: the CNMI-only restriction applies to EVS-TAP, not ESTA. Medical treatment is a permitted purpose under the US Visa Waiver Program when all eligibility and admission requirements are met. Confirm that the planned treatment fits the authorised stay; neither approval guarantees admission. Travel primarily to give birth to obtain US citizenship for a child is not a permitted visitor-visa purpose.
Is this website the treating hospital?
This website provides fertility information and consultation coordination; medical care is delivered by the receiving institution.

Confirm the institution, physician, medical payment recipient and coordination scope. Diagnosis, prescriptions, retrieval, laboratory procedures and transfer are performed by the receiving medical team.
Which services can I enquire about?
IVF, ICSI, egg or sperm freezing, donor resources and third-party family-building.
Existing-embryo transfers and single or LGBTQ+ family plans can also be discussed. Availability, eligibility, resources, documents and waiting times need individual confirmation.
How much should I budget for IVF?
The fee tool’s default combination is $26,100–31,100, subject to an individual written quotation.

It combines retrieval/culture $15,000, medication $3,000–8,000, anaesthesia $800, ICSI $1,800, freezing $1,000 and one FET $4,500. Initial tests, transfer medication, annual storage, travel, accommodation and extra treatment are excluded. ICSI is not required for everyone.
Does $15,000 include the entire IVF treatment?
No. It is the base reference for retrieval and embryo culture.
Stimulation medication, anaesthesia, ICSI, freezing, PGT, transfer and travel or accommodation are additional. Compare identical scopes and service counts before comparing totals.
How long does an IVF cycle take?
A complete cycle is commonly around 3–6 weeks; that is not necessarily your time in Saipan.

The NHS describes a 3–6 week cycle reference, including approximately two weeks of stimulation. Preparation, culture and transfer arrangements affect timing, and frozen transfer may be a separate stage. Obtain your personal dates before booking.
Is ICSI always more successful than conventional IVF?
No. Evidence does not support using ICSI as a universal success-rate add-on.

An ASRM 2026 committee opinion cites a trial of 2,387 couples without severe male-factor infertility: live birth was 33.8% with ICSI and 36.6% with conventional IVF, without a statistically significant difference. These are study results, not Saipan clinic success rates.
Can I enquire without examination reports?
Yes. You do not need to arrange a complete set of tests before the first enquiry.

Share your interests, treatment history, departure city and preferred timing. The receiving clinician confirms which reports are accepted, their validity and additional tests. Use the clinic’s confirmed channel for full records.
Must retrieval and transfer happen during the same visit?
No. Retrieval and transfer can be arranged in separate stages.

A fresh transfer may occur during the retrieval treatment stage. Frozen transfer or waiting for test results usually requires later preparation. The number of visits and duration depend on your individual plan.

form.title: Write your consultation questions
form.intro: Generate a draft, then review and send it in your own email application. No email is sent by this website.
form.subject: Subject
form.failed: Please select and copy the text manually.
form.changed: Your details changed. Please generate a new draft.
form.unsent: NOT SENT — Review and send the draft in your email application, or copy the text to your own email.
form.note: Do not include identity-document numbers or complete medical records. Confirm a suitable channel with the institution first.
form.templateText:
Hello, I would like to ask:
1. Is a remote first consultation available, how is it booked, and what is the fee?
2. Which existing reports are needed and how recent must they be?
3. How are treatment dates and the number of visits determined?
4. Can you provide the included services, additional costs and cancellation terms in writing?

budget.title: Build your reference budget
budget.failed: Select and copy the budget text manually.
budget.excluded: Excluded: initial tests, transfer medication, travel, accommodation, extra cycles, complications and unselected items.
budget.warning: ICSI and PGT-A are not required for everyone. A cycle does not guarantee a transferable embryo or pregnancy.
